Question: What is something no one will tell you about investing in blue chip stocks?
Answer: The story of some blue chip stocks: Market is full of success stories. Stories of stock prices moving to stratospheric high levels. Some people then come up with stories of an investor going into coma and finally dying and the son inheriting a large number of WIPRO, INFY, RELIANCE or EICHERMOT, type of shares. I have heard the story hundreds of times. Maybe there are few people who actually made those kind of gains. Today, we shall talk about the story that nobody likes to tell. Old timers will remember the tagline on the advertisements for SHOLAY — one of the most successful Hindi movie —— Greatest Story Ever Told. Today let us tell —- The Story Never Told The story of Yes Bank: Just two years ago it was among the bluest of the blue chips. Today it is downgraded and down in the dumps. It went out of NIFTY index, out of BANKNIFTY index and finally NSE took it out of Futures & Options segment. The big FIIs have moved out of the stock. Few big banks who were forced to buy the stock by the government are keeping it alive and eternally hopeful retail investors still keep buying it. Nobody told the investors to get out when it fell to Rs. 250 from Rs. 400 level. Nobody advised them to exit when it went below Rs. 200. Experts on TV were still discussing the move back to Rs. 300 and upward when the new CEO came in early in 2019. Nobody had a clue as to what was cooking. And if someone knew anything, surely it was never told. Instead you were told that Rakesh Jhunjhunuwala has bought a stake at Rs. 68.00. So what? The journey did not stop there and may continue further. From Rs. 404 on August 20, 2018, it crashed to Rs. 5.65 on March 06, 2020 and traded at Rs. 13.30 on October 23, 2020. Jaiprakash Associates: What? What stock are we talking about? Believe me, it was considered as a blue chip in the year 2008. Then it started losing value. Experts should have seen the trouble and talked about it. No, that does not happen. They were busy talking about revival and getting back to highs again. We get this kind of news: Rakesh Jhunjhunwala buys 3 crore shares in JP Associates; stock price jumps 10% This gentleman picks up the shares at Rs. 18.37 per share. Few years back he had bought at Rs. 26.00. Retail investors get lured. They think that big money is always right. To their dismay they find out that path to success is not found by following someone. This is the stock price two year after the above news: Rs. 3.75 is what it is today. Market does not care for anyone. Nobody talks about this story. Anil Ambani Group Stocks: Do not jump at me and tell that these were not blue chip stocks. They were blue chips before they were not. It is hard to believe today that Reliance Communications was among the top 10 NIFTY stocks in early 2008. It is equally hard to believe that Reliance Capital had traded above Rs. 2900 in its heady days. It is again hard to believe that fall like the one in Reliance Power is actually possible. Today, these stocks have achieved junk status. People tell you not to touch them. Two years ago, there was no one telling that. Maybe someone was —- only that happened to be yours truly. But I am no expert. Have a look for yourself as to how the mighty have fallen: Reliance Capital: Reliance Power: This was the stock with the most oversubscribed IPO ever till 2008. It made a low of Rs. 1.00 this year. Draw your own conclusions about the wealth destruction. Reliance Communication: Those who ask the kind of question —- The stock is down to Rs. 50 from Rs. 200. How much further can it fall? They will find their answer in this stock. From Rs. 844.70 to Rs. 0.50. Need another horror story. Himachal Futuristics: Another forgotten name. It was a darling of the investors in the dotcom boom days of 1999–2000. The stock saw its heady days before the dotcom bubble burst. It made its low in October 2008 and since then it is a stock that goes nowhere. Public memory is short. Specially about such stories of failure. Let us see how spectacular the failure was: From Rs. 2578 to Rs. 5.95. These were some horror stories. There are more but theme is the same, so numbers will not change the message. To Summarize: What no one tell you about blue chips is that they do not remain like that forever. Technology changes, poor management, fraud and public perception can make even the brightest of the blues to lose their sheen. In these stocks, chips have fallen and investors have been having the blues looking at their loss. One has to exit at the first sign of trouble and not get deluded by one big investor buying a stake in the company. We know that SBI bought stake in Kingfisher Airlines and Reliance Communications. That did not stop the stocks becoming worthless. There is a lesson to be learnt from such stories. Let us learn that. Thanks for reading. Pramod Kumar's answer to What stock should I never purchase? Question: Do you think there is any chance of the NIFTY to stoop down to 9,000 levels in June or July?
Answer: Guesswork. Crystal gazing. Prediction. Call it whatever. I could say yes and give a lot of reasons and be wrong. Or I maybe right with the wrong reasoning. Markets can make us look stupid all the time. Let us always remember this fact. Market is volatile and undecided about the direction presently. We saw this on Friday, June 12, 2020: The low point of the day was at 9544.35 and it moved up from there to close at 9972.90. Some call it resilience of our markets, some say NIFTY has a very strong support at 9500 levels and now it should sustain above this level. This is the kind of talk we listen to everyday. Nobody is wiser for it and nobody makes money from this. We had a similar move ( on a much bigger scale ) on March 13, 2020. NIFTY had hit the lower circuit at 10% fall on that day. I have saved the image somewhere to remember that day. Nifty went down to 8555.15. A loss of more than 10%. Trading was halted for 45 minutes as NIFTY cracked 10%. Once the trading resumed, NIFTY started recovering after the initial hiccup and — What A Recovery. It made a high of 10159.40. From 9590 to 8555 and then to 10159. This ride surely beats any high adrenaline roller coaster ride. The gap between the low and high point was 1604 points. Considering the low point as the base, the day saw a recovery of 18.75%. Why the comparison?: We listened to the same song on that day. NIFTY has made a bottom. It is resilient and see how it recovered. Remember, the coronavirus scare was just a news. Our trains were running, people were travelling and businesses had not closed. Lock down was not even in thinking at that time. Within few days NIFTY had made a low of 7511. Then came the lock down on March 25 and the markets did not care for it. The low of 7511.10 was made on March 24 and after the announcement of lock down NIFTY closed at 8317.85 on March 25. Irrational? Yes. But that is the reality of the market. What lies ahead?: Market has gone up very significantly in April. Gave up a little part of the gain in May and is consolidating in June. The current level is almost same as the level on March 13, 2020 when the people expected that the worst was over. I expect similar move from here. Maybe not as big a move as in March but a down move all the same. Yes, a move to 9000 is very likely in June or July 2020. Brace yourself for the roller coaster hurtling down. Have your positions hedged wisely. If the down move does not happen, nothing is lost. If it really comes about, one saves a fortune. Thanks for reading.

Question: Which stocks are good for a long-term investment if I invest 10,000 Rs. monthly, only in the stock market?
Answer: Good long term investments in stock market: My regular readers know that I generally talk about stocks to avoid. Not getting caught up in bad stocks is equally important as finding good stocks and investing in them. This question is about Rs. 10000 every month over a period of time. It is a good and consistent way to investment. The easiest advice would be to go for a blue chip mutual fund through systematic investment plan ( SIP ). Nothing is wrong with that approach. It is easily done and over a long period of time the results are good. But it is like eating food cooked by someone else. Taste may be good but the recipe is not known to us. Let us cook our own dish. Stock Selection: I have a very simple approach to stock selection. For good food, we need good ingredients. These are the top 10 stocks in NIFTY index by weight: We see that there are 3 banking stocks in the top 10. That is too much money in one sector even when we are looking at the top stocks in the market. We take only 2 out of them and make a portfolio of 9 top stocks. Rs. 10000 is not such a big amount that we can buy every stock every month. We do that by rotation. Buy 45 shares of ITC one month, 18 shares of ICICIBABK in the next month, 7 shares of HDFCBANK followed by 5 shares of RELIANCE and so on. This has to be done on regular basis. Results: When the ingredients are good, the food is bound to be nutritious unless we spoil it by over cooking. Let us not do that. Let the pot simmer and cook on the low heat. Time in the market is more important than timing in the market. Unfortunately, most of us are looking to get the timing right and failing at that. Let us see how these stocks performed over last 52 weeks ( 1 year ): We can see that NIFTY gained 16.94% over 365 days. Our portfolio should do better than that on average basis. We have good out performance by INFY ( 75% ) , TCS ( 44% ), RELIANCE ( 27% ), HINDUNILVR. HDFCBANK and KOTAKBANK have not kept pace with NIFTY. In fact banking sector has lagged the market significantly. These kind of differences keep on happening. That is what brings taste to the cooked food. If all the stocks make uniform moves, the taste will be bland. ITC has been a loser for the year by 10%. Maybe that is the stock that is likely to do well in the next one year. This kind of SIP is our own mutual fund. And very likely to succeed. One of the readers had asked me exactly this question over phone few months ago. And this is what I had told him at that time. I hope your dish turns out nice and tasty with these ingredients. It will be appropriate to put a disclaimer here: I am not an advisor for investment or wealth management. What is written above is just my views on the question asked. Thanks for reading. Images : NSE website

Question: How much time do you think the Indian market will take to get back to normal?
Answer: How much time do you think the Indian market will take to get back to normal?: What is normal? Market always moving upward is not normal. Market always moving down is not normal. Big moves everyday is not normal. Very small moves everyday is not normal. All the above statements are wrong. Let us see what the market has been doing over last 3 months: This is NIFTY 50 Chart for 3 month period. It fell from 12000 levels to almost 7500 —- a fall of 37.5%. It has risen from 7500 levels to 9300 levels —- a rise of 24%. From this point it may either go up or go down again — no one can predict that. All this is normal. Market is about perceptions and action in the market is swift. At times it looks wrong and overdone but market is always right. It is a trader or investor who is wrong. There is a virus which has disrupted the economy all over the world. At first we will get out of the present bad situation. The road to recovery will be tough and progress slow. Some businesses will never recover and just close. Market will reflect all that. Market reaction will be painful at some time and euphoric at other times. And everything is considered normal. Market is always right. Thanks for reading. Images : Fyers Web and Google Images

Question: What should Indian investors be most worried about for 2019?
Answer: What should Indian Investors be most worried about for 2019 ? : Indian investors should worry about the hype and hoopla surrounding the current high levels of SENSEX and NIFTY. Indian investors should check the facts and not be taken in by the positive talks on TV shows. Indian investors should look at the numbers and then decide what is good or bad. Some of the facts : NIFTY Index went up 12% over last 365 days. Out of 50 stocks in the index, 22 were losers for the year some as much as by 57%. Actually NSE website shows 25 losers but TCS, INFY and BRITANNIA are wrongly shown as the effect of bonus/split is not considered. Then there is NIFTY NEXT 50 Index. Here the number of losers is 29 out of 50. So out of 100 prominent stocks, 51 were on the losing side for the year. But the 100 stocks are not the entire market. If we look at NIFTY MIDCAP 250 and NIFTY SMALL CAP 250 also, we find that 357 out of 500 stocks were losers for the year. This gives us the real picture. Out of 600 stocks in NIFTY 50, NIFTY NEXT 50 and MID CAP and SMALL CAP Index, 408 lost money during the year. And with 408 stocks out of 600 in the red , we are supposed to believe that our stock markets are in good health and every thing is fine. This is how the hype is marketed. This is how the blatant lies are sold to the public. And we are guilty of being gullible. We do not do our home work and then wonder what hit us. To Summarize : Indian Investor should check the facts about the strength or weakness in the market. Markets do go up in the long run but many stocks fall by the way side. NIFTY has gone up 12% in one year but many stocks have lost 80–90% in the same period. Gain in NIFTY is of no consolation to those invested in these stocks. And be prepared for the day when the truth will overtake the lies being marketed now. Truth hits real hard. Thanks for reading. Images : NSE Website and Google Images
